argument: Building on Kant's phenomena/noumena distinction, Schopenhauer questions the assumption that the noumenal 'thing in itself' contains separate plural things, and argues introspection gives us a unique 'subterranean passage' into that reality via the self. There he finds not reason but a blind, restless striving he calls the Will, which he generalizes into a single cosmic force underlying all of reality — implying that suffering is universal and, since we are ultimately one, is in effect our own. Applied to human life, this reveals love and the drive toward marriage and children as an elaborate scam: an irrational, temporary insanity the Will manufactures to secure reproduction, which is why passionate love and lasting compatibility so rarely coincide, and why happiness and love remain separate, non-identical goals.
keyIdeas: Kant's phenomena/noumena distinction: the mind organizes raw sense data via built-in categories into experienced phenomena, while the 'thing in itself' (noumena), independent of that processing, is permanently inaccessible.

Schopenhauer questions whether plurality is a feature of reality itself or merely imposed on it by human perception (space, time, causality), and argues introspection gives us a unique 'subterranean passage' into that reality via the self, since we have direct, intimate access to at least one thing-in-itself: ourselves.

What introspection reveals is the Will: a subconscious, restless striving underlying all action, always wanting the next thing, which Schopenhauer generalizes into a single blind, non-rational force underlying all of reality, human and non-human alike.

The dark implication of this monism: since all beings are one Will restlessly striving, and survival requires consuming other striving beings, existence necessarily involves the Will 'cannibalizing' itself, and because we are ultimately one, all suffering witnessed is, in effect, our own.

People believe they pursue marriage and children rationally, but for Schopenhauer love is the irrational, temporary 'insanity' the Will manufactures to compel reproduction; attraction tracks complementary traits (tall paired with short, meek with courageous) aimed at balanced offspring rather than genuine compatibility, which is why he compares marrying for passionate love to blindly reaching into a 'sack of snakes' hoping to find an eel.

terms.def: Kant's distinction between the world as experienced through the mind's categories and the 'thing in itself,' independent of that processing.
Schopenhauer's name for the blind, restless, non-rational striving he finds through introspection and generalizes into the single force underlying all of reality.
The view that everything in the universe is a manifestation of one underlying Will, apparently separate only because of how perception structures experience.
The force subconsciously compelling beings toward survival and reproduction, manifesting in humans as the irrational feeling of romantic love.
Schopenhauer's image for marrying based on passionate love: blindly reaching in hoping for compatibility (an eel) but usually finding mismatch (a snake).
